description: A small non-modal panel a trigger opens, holding content of the consumer's own: a filter form with its Apply button, a pair of dates, a paragraph that explains a figure. The page behind it stays usable, nothing is trapped, and the panel escapes a clipping ancestor. A popover is not a menu of actions and not a hover description.

trigger.description: The control that opens the panel. The consumer draws it -- a secondary ArenaButton, an ArenaIconButton -- so it is a slot, and it carries its own accessible name. The slot holds one element that takes focus.

content.description: What the panel holds: a short form, a pair of fields, a paragraph. The content fills the panel and never replaces it: the surface, its padding and its edge are Arena's.

label.description: Names the panel for assistive technology: what it holds, not that it is a panel. Required, and guarded at runtime: a dialog with no accessible name is announced unlabelled, and the trigger's own name says what opens it, never what the panel is for. "Filters", not "Popover".

open.description: Whether the panel is shown. The consumer owns it: the component asks to change it through openChange and never changes it by itself, so content inside the panel can close it, an Apply button included.

align.description: Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with.

openChange.description: The panel asks to be shown or hidden, carrying the state it asks for: the trigger was pressed, Escape was pressed while it was the topmost panel, a press landed outside it, or Tab left it. The panel moves only when open does.
